commit.message:
README: the fork on 0.1.40.2 - measured against stock 0.1.40.2, the CPU share and its PRs

best is Strata v0.1.40.2 plus the fork's changes. The table is 2026-10-07's: the coding agent's conversation 137.4 s
stock against 128.7 s the fork on two GPUs (126.1 against 116.8 s on the RTX 5070 Ti alone), short prompts 1.3-1.9x
as fast. Hardin22's two changes are upstream since 0.1.40.2; #1414 is in 0.1.41, #1416 open. The 0.1.40.1 table's
-13% had stock reading with STRATA_PF_FUSED=1; that note stays.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

prefill: CPU assist's pool is set_assist_pool; one experts_cpu and one cpu_jobs

Upstream 0.1.40.2's STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE added a Prefill::set_cpu_pool, a PrefillStats::experts_cpu
and an Impl::cpu_jobs with the same names as CPU assist's.  The two setters stay apart (upstream sets
its pool on one GPU without --batch only; CPU assist's also on a layer split's stages, with
STRATA_SPLIT_CPU_ASSIST=1), so the fork's is renamed; the counter and the job list are shared - the
two never run in one chunk.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge upstream v0.1.40.2 into the fork's best

Upstream 0.1.40.2 (e8ca9af, 242 commits on 0.1.40.1) took Hardin22's two commits this branch
carried: the AVX2 Q8_K activation quantizer (#851) and the pipelined windows beside the
asynchronous adaptive tier (#905); their code is upstream's now (one copy of the quantizer's
declaration; STRATA_PIPELINE_ADAPT_ASYNC read as upstream reads it).

Kept from the fork: CPU assist (and on a layer split's stages) and the pipelined decode's
lookahead (the verified path served first, lookup_next / lkany, the gate at 0.10).

Upstream's own STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE (opt-in, chunks under 1,024 tokens, one GPU) and
CPU assist hand a staged chunk's experts to the same CPU pool: CPU assist stands down when
STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE is set, so each can be measured alone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
setup: engine versions compare all four numbers and MIN_ENGINE is 0.1.40.2, so an installed 0.1.40 engine is replaced by the new one

sycl: the sampler's top_p/temperature tail accumulates in float (FP64 is emulated on Arc Alchemist); B70 IQ3_S findings in docs/INTEL.md

samp_acc_t is float by default (-DSTRATA_SYCL_SAMPLER_FP64=1 keeps the reference's double). On an Arc A750 one row of the
tail cost 451 us in double and 20 us in float; a sampled decode ran at 7.62 -> 8.10 tok/s (medians of 5 interleaved
pairs, runs 7.1-9.2). sampler_parity: 0 failures on the A750 (JIT build) and on the B70; both cards' 10-prompt gates pass
10 of 10, and the B70 gate's sampled cases pick the same tokens as before. Of the kernels that use double, only the
sampler runs on a native pack (the router, combine, gate and norm kernels there are float).

Probes: sycl/probe/fp64_cost.cpp (FP64 against float in the small reduction kernels), gemm_vary.cpp.
docs/INTEL.md: the aliased-pages bug, NO_HOST, the prompt-chunking numbers, draft-length sweep, FP64 and XMX findings;
docs/INTEL_ARC.md: a row for the B70/A750 runs.
docs: STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE (opt-in) with the measured prompt times and its output difference

prefill: STRATA_DBG_NAN does not count the CPU-share rows of GU and H (the GPU never writes them)

With STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE on, the last rows_cpu rows of GU and H hold whatever the buffer held before; the check read
them and reported them as non-finite (about 1 in 256 garbage floats), with Dm and the layer output clean.

prefill: the CPU-share thread takes no ExpertSource call (blobs taken on the prefill thread, blob_stable)

blob() bumps a plain reads_ counter and, for a file source, its mapped/staged paths; calling it from the share's
thread raced with the prefill thread's own blob_stable()/pinned() calls (the streamed experts). The blobs of the CPU's
experts are now taken before the thread starts, so the thread reads only the arena bytes, the activations and the
grouping tables, none of which the prefill thread writes until the thread is joined.

prefill: STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=auto hands a small chunk's least-routed experts to the idle CPU pool

A chunk below stream_all_min() (1,024 tokens: an agent's tool result, a test's
output) streams every routed expert outside VRAM over PCIe while the decode CPU
pool sits idle and the arena holds the same experts in RAM.  Opt-in,
STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=auto|x:
- the non-resident experts routed by at most MAXT of the chunk's tokens,
  fewest first, run on the pool on a thread while the GPU streams and runs the
  rest; their unweighted rows go to Dm's tail (as a peer GPU's do) and the
  combine weights them as any other row;
- auto: the share measured, each layer's CPU time per expert and the GPU's per
  streamed expert (CUDA events around its expert work, read after the next
  layer's routing sync), and the next layers hand the CPU g / (c + g), where
  both end together - a small CPU takes a small share;
- Q2_0 layers take the pool's Q2_0 kernels' activations (ActQ, as decode's),
  i-quant layers the native vec_dot type.

Serve without batch slots and generate, one GPU.  Unset (the default): no
expert moves, byte-identical to v0.1.39 (IQ2_XS 600 and 2,100 tokens, fixed
cache, logits and 32 tokens).

RTX 5090 + 9950X3D, 600-token prompts, ms (off / auto):
- UD-Q4_K_XL: 1,548 / 1,369, 1,528 / 1,296 (share 0.65; KL between 0.006);
- Q2_0: 472 / 445, 491 / 448;
- IQ2_XS: 493 / 481, 502 / 460, 527 / 529; 250 tokens 424 / 355, 402 / 382,
  379 / 367 (KL to STRATA_PREFILL_MMQ=0 0.0053 off, 0.0080 auto);
- IQ2_XS on 2 AVX2 workers (emulated): 512 / 487 (share 0.49).
